skill.name: agile-design-doc
skill.description: Creates concise, MVP-focused design documents after reviewing a project's technology stack, reusable components, workflows, implementation approach, data models, and interfaces.
skill.summary: Turn feature requirements and repository context into a focused technical design for agile delivery.
skill.author: AriesYB

content.value_statement: Feature teams often lose time in lengthy or incomplete technical planning. This skill creates concise, repository-aware design documents focused on MVP delivery.
actual_capabilities: Reviews project configuration, structure, documentation, and reusable components before proposing a design.
Defines design goals and a concise list of MVP features.
Creates Mermaid sequence diagrams for major interaction flows.
Describes implementation approaches, key methods, and technical challenges.
Documents new or changed data models and API interfaces.
Checks the result for focus, technical alignment, reuse, and unnecessary scope.
limitations: Requires repository access or user-provided context for technology-specific recommendations.
Produces design guidance and illustrative examples, not production-ready implementation.
Does not validate runtime behavior, performance, or deployment outcomes.
Deliberately postpones secondary features and uncommon edge cases beyond the MVP.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Convert feature requirements into goals, interactions, implementation steps, models, and interfaces that support an MVP release.

use_cases.title: Align an Agile Delivery Team
use_cases.description: Create a compact design reference that gives developers and product staff a shared technical scope.

use_cases.title: Extend an Existing Service
use_cases.description: Review the current stack and components before designing a compatible module that reuses established project patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an MVP-focused design document for [feature]. Include goals, a short feature list, and the main interaction flow.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the feature idea is clear but implementation planning has not started.

prompt_templates.title: Design from Repository Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository and design [feature]. Identify the technology stack and reusable components before proposing implementation details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the design must match an existing codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Define Service Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design [feature] for this service. Include Mermaid interactions, changed data models, API definitions, key methods, and technical challenges.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for backend features that change several service boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Scope and Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a focused design for [feature] under [constraints]. Separate MVP scope from later work and explain reuse, tradeoffs, risks, and assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when architecture choices, constraints, or delivery scope require explicit decisions.

output_examples.input: Design passwordless sign-in for an existing web application using its current session service.
output_examples.output: A concise design covering sign-in goals, email-link flow, session-service reuse, token handling, endpoint changes, and deferred enhancements.

output_examples.input: Plan an order-status notification module for a service that already uses a message queue.
output: Mermaid sequence for order, queue, worker, and provider interactions
Implementation notes for existing queue components

output_examples.input: Add team invitations to an existing SaaS application with a two-week delivery limit.
output_examples.output: A repository-aligned design that defines invitation scope, user flow, data changes, endpoints, implementation methods, assumptions, and later improvements.

best_practices: Provide the feature goal, delivery constraints, and relevant repository context.
Confirm which existing components and conventions the design should reuse.
Review assumptions and deferred items with engineering and product stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Do not request a stack-specific design without repository access or technology details.
Do not treat illustrative methods as tested production code.
Do not expand optional features into the MVP without an explicit delivery need.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the feature goal, current system context, constraints, and repository access when available.

faq.question: Does the skill inspect an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews configuration, source structure, documentation, and reusable components when those files are available.

faq.question: What sections can the design include?
faq.answer: It can include goals, features, interactions, implementation details, key methods, technical challenges, models, and interfaces.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides illustrative code for key methods, but implementation and testing remain separate tasks.

faq.question: How does it prevent excessive scope?
faq.answer: It prioritizes core functionality, marks optional work for later iterations, and checks for unnecessary sections or features.

faq.question: Can it work when requirements are incomplete?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews available project context, asks focused questions, and records reasonable assumptions in the document.
